end.summary:
- Food miles were defined as the full distance from farm to plate, not only shop to home.
- Rohan compared nearer and farther foods using distance travelled.
- They linked greater distance with more petrol/diesel use and reduced freshness.
- They identified the food from 10 km away as having fewer food miles.
- The initial shop-to-home mix-up was corrected later in the lesson; pollution and refrigeration effects remained partly unexplained.
end.parentNote: Asha practised defining food miles and comparing foods by travel distance, fuel use, and freshness. Rohan used the full journey from farm to plate to correct the shop-to-home mix-up. At home, ask them to trace one food’s journey and discuss how distance may affect fuel use, pollution, and freshness.
